title: Exact adaptive queries for pointwise decision sufficiency
description:
This note answers the deployment-time adaptive query question in Ye, Amin and Özdağlar’s COLT 2026 proceedings, §7, paper page 13. For a bounded rational linear program and an open rational polyhedral cost prior, it computes the exact minimum worst-case number of deterministic real linear queries needed to return a common optimizer for the set of costs still consistent with the observed answers. It also constructs an optimal semialgebraic policy.

The proof represents each finite query history by its exact cost fiber. A history wins at depth zero when one feasible point is optimal throughout the fiber. A history wins at the next depth if it already wins at zero or if it admits a query whose every feasible answer leaves a winning shorter history. Real quantifier elimination decides these predicates, and cylindrical decomposition selects policy actions. The proof gives no efficient runtime or bit-complexity claim.

For every m ≥ 2, a nondegenerate cube has exactly two worst-case adaptive queries and exactly m fixed queries. A first measurement chooses at most one of several disjoint cost windows where an unresolved sign can affect the optimum. A fixed dataset must measure all m independent sign-change directions. The gap persists on a bounded rational box, with a separate bounded ellipsoid extension.

The deposit includes the PDF, LaTeX source, bibliography, citation metadata, an evidence archive and checksums. The exact replay tests the polyhedral, bounded-box and ellipsoid cases, and the 3D explorer responds to changes in the query transcript. Internally reviewed. External peer review is pending.

ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proofs, bounded-prior supplement and original replay under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, extended replay and worked illustration. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity.
